name: Scribe
desc: You spent formative years in a scriptorium, a monastery dedicated to the preservation of knowledge, or a government agency, where you learned to write with a clear hand and produce finely written texts. Perhaps you scribed government documents or copied tomes of literature. You might have some skill as a writer of poetry, narrative, or scholarly research.

feature.name: Skilled
desc: You have exceptionally broad learning. You gain proficiency in any combination of three skills or tools of your choice.

traits: I use polysyllabic words that convey the impression of great erudition.
I'm a perfectionist who can't finish a task until it's flawless.
I've read every book in the world's greatest libraries — or I like to boast that I have.
I'm used to helping out those who aren't as bright as I am.
There's nothing I like more than a good mystery.
I am horribly, horribly awkward in social situations.
I speak slowly when talking to people who don't understand the intricacies of my work.
I'm convinced that people are always trying to steal my research.
ideals: Knowledge. The path to power and self-improvement is through knowledge. (Neutral)
Accuracy. Truth is the most important thing; we must record it faithfully. (Lawful)
Creativity. The written word is a tool for expression and change. (Chaotic)
Power. Information is power, and I intend to have it all. (Evil)
Preservation. We must protect the records of the past for the future. (Any)
Self-Improvement. The goal of study is the betterment of oneself. (Any)
bonds: I work to preserve a library, university, or scriptorium.
My life's work is a series of tomes related to a specific field of lore.
I have an ancient text that holds terrible secrets that must not fall into the wrong hands.
I'm trying to find the one who burned down my master's library.
I owe my education to a generous benefactor who I hope to make proud.
Everything I do is for the pursuit of truth.
flaws: I overlook obvious solutions in favor of complicated ones.
I can't keep a secret to save my life, or anyone else's.
I am easily distracted by the promise of new information.
I speak without really thinking through my words, step on toes, and irritate people.
Unlocking an ancient mystery is worth the price of a civilization.
I judge others harshly based on their literacy and grammar.
